title: Establish PRD interlock matrix for staged model pinning & acceptance automation
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Context: The PRD for staged model pinning introduces a mechanism for locking a model version per-tenant during rollouts and fallbacks. This ticket formalizes the cross-team acceptance matrix and automates the signoff path so Eng/Design/Legal can validate readiness without blocking releases. Goals: 1) Define clear acceptance lanes and owners for each verification domain (runtime perf, API contract, UX surface, privacy/data residency, telemetry opt-in). 2) Produce an automated checklist that gates can query (OK status per owner). 3) Capture review artifacts and roll-forward/rollback criteria. Scope: - Included: acceptance criteria, review owners, required artifacts, automation hooks for CI/CD, runbook for rollback. - Excluded: implementation work for runtime kernel selection or full telemetry ingestion pipeline (those are separate ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Each lane (Engineering, Design, Legal/Privacy, SRE) has an assigned owner and a documented OK/NeedsFollowUp/Blocked signal
A minimal machine-readable acceptance payload (JSON) is specified and stored in the PRD, with clear field definitions for 'owner', 'status', 'evidence_link', 'timestamp'
Automation hook exists to read acceptance payload during release runs and fail the release when any lane is Blocked
Design provides annotated screens and a migration UX doc for pinned model state and admin override flows
Legal confirms allowed data flows for model version telemetry and signs off on residency restrictions for EU customers
Performance SLOs defined for pinned model paths (p50/p95 latency and token cost), with thresholds and monitoring dashboards linked
Rollback criteria enumerated (e.g., quality regressions on sentinel prompts, >10% error rate increase, region-wide capacity drop) and owner for escalation identified
A checklist of artifacts (PRD section links, Figma file, e2e test run link, privacy README, telemetry dashboard) is present in the PR and referenced by the acceptance payload
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Decided to use a lightweight JSON acceptance payload instead of a monolithic spreadsheet to enable CI integration (owner: Marisol Vega).
